meta.note: Sources were found by web search in October 2026, with peer-reviewed country examples first. One-line takeaways are in our own words; where marked, they are based on the abstract or publisher page only. Items marked as not read were listed from titles only.

sources.title: Antimicrobial resistance: report of the Director-General to WHA77 and the UNGA high-level meeting (2024)
sources.takeaway: Uses TrACSS 2023 (177 countries): 68% implement some elements of their plan, 27% have a costed and monitored plan, 11% have budget provisions; fewer than 40% have a nationwide IPC programme aligned with WHO core components; implementation and financing lag behind plan development.

sources.title: Monitoring progress on antimicrobial resistance response in the WHO African Region: insights from the TrACSS 2021. Results for the Human Health Sector
sources.authors: Gahimbare L, Mwamelo AJ, Ahmed YA, et al.
sources.journal: Journal of Public Health in Africa 14(11)
sources.takeaway: Secondary analysis of 41 countries: 85% had a plan, but only 37% had a functional multisectoral group and 32% a national system to monitor antimicrobial use; the authors call for functional One Health governance, funding and clear monitoring.

sources.title: 2025 edition of global survey to track antimicrobial resistance launches
sources.takeaway: Describes who runs the survey, the record 2024 response (186 countries) and the target of a 95% submission rate by 2030.

sources.title: Global Database for Tracking AMR Country Self-Assessment Survey (TrACSS)
sources.takeaway: Country pages with results over the years and a download of the questionnaire.
sources.note: Questionnaire itself not opened for this page.

sources.title: Monitoring global progress on antimicrobial resistance: Tripartite AMR country self-assessment survey (TrACSS) 2019-2020
sources.takeaway: Earlier global analysis of the survey results.
sources.note: Contents not read; listed from the title.

sources.title: Tripartite AMR Country Self-Assessment Survey (TrACSS) 2018-2019
sources.takeaway: Earlier version of the survey and its results.
sources.note: Contents not read; listed from the title.

sources.title: Reduction of veterinary antimicrobial use in the Netherlands. The Dutch success model
sources.authors: Speksnijder DC, Mevius DJ, Bruschke CJ, Wagenaar JA
sources.takeaway: A public-private approach with national reduction targets, an independent authority that benchmarks farms and veterinarians on use, mandatory recording and restrictions on critically important antibiotics brought a large fall in veterinary antibiotic sales.
sources.note: Takeaway based on the abstract or publisher page; full text not read.

sources.title: Close to a decade of decrease in antimicrobial usage in Danish pig production: evaluating the effect of the Yellow Card scheme
sources.takeaway: Herd-level thresholds with sanctions for high users (Yellow Card, 2010) coincided with a fall of about half in use in high-consuming weaner and finisher herds within a year; observational design, so not proof of cause.

sources.title: Effectiveness of alternative measures to reduce antimicrobial usage in pig production in four European countries
sources.authors: Raasch S, Collineau L, Postma M, et al.
sources.takeaway: Farm-specific packages (biosecurity, vaccination, management, feed) in 68 herds cut treatment incidence by about 35%, more in weaned pigs, without major harm to pig health.

sources.title: Significant reduction of antibiotic use in the community after a nationwide campaign in France, 2002-2007
sources.authors: Sabuncu E, David J, Bernède-Bauduin C, et al.
sources.takeaway: The national campaign “Les antibiotiques c'est pas automatique” was followed by a marked fall in outpatient antibiotic prescriptions, largest in young children.
sources.note: Takeaway based on the abstract or publisher page; full text not read.

sources.title: Provision of social norm feedback to high prescribers of antibiotics in general practice: a pragmatic national randomised controlled trial
sources.authors: Hallsworth M, Chadborn T, Sallis A, et al.
sources.takeaway: A letter from the Chief Medical Officer telling the highest-prescribing practices they prescribed more than most peers cut their antibiotic prescribing by about 3% over six months, at very low cost: an example of evidence-based behaviour change (question 2.21).
sources.note: Takeaway based on the abstract or publisher page; full text not read.

sources.title: Evaluation of e-Bug, an educational pack, teaching about prudent antibiotic use and hygiene, in the Czech Republic, France and England
sources.authors: Lecky DM, McNulty CAM, Touboul P, et al.
sources.takeaway: School pack on microbes, hygiene and antibiotics improved pupils' knowledge; an example for youth education (question 2.25).
sources.note: Title and journal from the publisher listing; takeaway not checked against the article.

sources.title: Lessons learnt during 20 years of the Swedish strategic programme against antibiotic resistance
sources.authors: Mölstad S, Löfmark S, Carlin K, et al.
sources.journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization 95
sources.takeaway: Strama combined a national coordinating body with local multidisciplinary groups in every county, prescribing data fed back to prescribers and treatment guidance; outpatient use fell while resistance stayed low.
sources.note: Takeaway based on the abstract or publisher page; full text not read.

sources.title: Thailand's national strategic plan on antimicrobial resistance: progress and challenges
sources.authors: Sumpradit N, Wongkongkathep S, Malathum K, et al.
sources.journal: Bulletin of the World Health Organization 99
sources.takeaway: Mid-term review of a plan with national targets for use and resistance: governance and some targets moved, others lagged, and the paper names what helped and what blocked progress.
sources.note: Takeaway based on the abstract or publisher page; full text not read.

sources.title: Kenya's National Action Plan on antimicrobial resistance: measuring implementation progress
sources.authors: Mukoko J, Wesangula E, Gitonga N, et al.
sources.takeaway: Of 85 planned activities, 29 were completed, 37 ongoing and 19 not started; human health moved faster than animal and crop sectors. Funding, cross-sector collaboration and laboratory supplies were the main obstacles and shaped the 2023-2027 plan.

sources.title: Interventions to improve antibiotic prescribing practices for hospital inpatients
sources.authors: Davey P, Marwick CA, Scott CL, et al.
sources.takeaway: Stewardship interventions in hospitals increase adherence to antibiotic policies and shorten treatment without raising mortality; enabling interventions (feedback, advice) add to restrictive ones.
sources.note: Takeaway based on the abstract or publisher page; full text not read.

sources.title: Evaluation of the national Cleanyourhands campaign to reduce Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia and Clostridium difficile infection in hospitals in England and Wales by improved hand hygiene
sources.authors: Stone SP, Fuller C, Savage J, et al.
sources.takeaway: A national hand-hygiene campaign raised soap and alcohol rub use; higher soap use was linked with lower C. difficile and higher rub use with lower MRSA bacteraemia, alongside other national measures.
sources.note: Takeaway based on the abstract or publisher page; full text not read.

sources.title: Nationwide intervention to contain carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae in Israeli hospitals
sources.authors: Schwaber MJ, Lev B, Israeli A, et al.
sources.takeaway: A national task force with mandatory reporting, isolation of carriers and dedicated staff, enforced by the ministry, brought a national CRE outbreak under control.
sources.note: Takeaway based on the abstract or publisher page; full text not read.

sources.title: Bacteriology testing and antimicrobial resistance detection capacity of national tiered laboratory networks in sub-Saharan Africa: an analysis from 14 countries
sources.authors: MAAP study group; Ondoa P, Kapoor G, et al.
sources.takeaway: 78% of 504 laboratories reported susceptibility testing, but in seven countries they reached under half of the population; 12 of 14 national action plans gave less than a fifth of their actions to testing capacity.

sources.title: Global monitoring of antimicrobial resistance based on metagenomics analyses of urban sewage
sources.authors: Hendriksen RS, Munk P, Njage P, et al.
sources.takeaway: Sewage from 74 cities showed clear regional differences in resistance genes, linked to sanitation and health factors; shows sewage as a cheap, ethically simple route to national and global AMR surveillance in the environment.
sources.note: Takeaway based on the abstract or publisher page; full text not read.

sources.title: Effluent from drug manufactures contains extremely high levels of pharmaceuticals
sources.authors: Larsson DGJ, de Pedro C, Paxeus N
sources.takeaway: Treated effluent from a plant serving antibiotic manufacturers near Hyderabad contained antibiotics at concentrations above therapeutic levels in blood; a founding case for controls on manufacturing discharges (questions 6.3 to 6.5).
sources.note: Takeaway based on the abstract or publisher page; full text not read.

sources.title: The use and impact of antibiotics in plant agriculture: a review
sources.authors: Batuman O, Britt-Ugartemendia K, Kunwar S, et al.
sources.takeaway: Reviews which antibiotics are used on crops (mainly streptomycin and oxytetracycline), where, how they are regulated and the evidence on resistance; useful for questions 5.2, 5.10 and 5.11.
sources.note: Listed from the title and publisher record; contents not read.

sources.title: A scoping review of disposal of unused medicines in take-back programs
sources.takeaway: Overview of how take-back schemes for unused medicines are organised and used.
sources.note: Contents not read; listed from the title.

sources.title: WHO costing and budgeting tool for national action plans on antimicrobial resistance
sources.takeaway: Tool to cost and budget a national action plan; relevant for the investment case (2.7) and financing (2.3.a level D).

sources.title: A one health priority research agenda for antimicrobial resistance
sources.takeaway: The research agenda the questionnaire points to for question 2.6.

sources.title: Guidelines on core components of infection prevention and control programmes at the national and acute health care facility level
sources.takeaway: The core components that question 3.14 measures against.

sources.title: The WHO AWaRe (Access, Watch, Reserve) antibiotic book
sources.takeaway: Guidance behind the AWaRe classification asked about in question 3.17.

sources.title: Global Antimicrobial Resistance and Use Surveillance System (GLASS)
sources.takeaway: WHO system for national reporting of resistance and use in humans; the reference for questions 3.2 and 3.5.

sources.title: ANIMUSE: WOAH database on antimicrobial agents intended for use in animals
sources.takeaway: Where countries report animal use data (questions 4.5.b and 4.6).

sources.title: FAO Assessment Tool for Laboratories and AMR Surveillance Systems (FAO-ATLASS)
sources.takeaway: The assessment tool named in question 5.7 for laboratory networks and surveillance in food and agriculture.

sources.title: The International FAO Antimicrobial Resistance Monitoring (InFARM) system: manual for implementation 2024
sources.takeaway: How to report animal and food AMR data to FAO (questions 5.6 and 5.6.a).

sources.title: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2020/1729 on the monitoring and reporting of AMR in zoonotic and commensal bacteria
sources.takeaway: The EU's harmonised monitoring of resistance in food-producing animals and meat; a worked example of what level E in 4.7 and 5.3 looks like.

sources.title: Guidance on wastewater and solid waste management for manufacturing of antibiotics
sources.takeaway: First WHO guidance with targets for antibiotic discharges from manufacturing.

sources.title: Towards a better and harmonized education in antimicrobial stewardship in European veterinary curricula
sources.takeaway: Survey of European veterinary schools on how stewardship is taught, with proposals for shared learning outcomes; a reference for question 4.1 level E (AMR systematically in curricula).
sources.note: Listed from the title and repository record; contents not read.

sources.title: Bracing for superbugs: strengthening environmental action in the One Health response to antimicrobial resistance
sources.takeaway: UNEP report on the environmental drivers of AMR (manufacturing, health care, agriculture and municipal waste) and the policy actions countries can take; the background for Section VI.
